note.after_visit_summary:
Mr. Darnell Whitaker, your symptoms of swollen ankles, weight gain, trouble walking, and needing extra pillows to sleep are due to a mild worsening of your heart failure. You have gained 7 pounds in a week and your heart's pumping strength is reduced. Recent salty foods and ibuprofen-like pain pills called naproxen likely made the extra fluid retention worse, so you must stop the naproxen.

Please take acetaminophen 650 mg up to 3 times a day for your knees instead. Your water pill, furosemide, will increase to 40 mg twice a day for the next 5 days, then go back to 40 mg once daily when your weight returns near 183 pounds. Take all your other heart medicines exactly as before.

Weigh yourself every morning and write it down. Stay under 2000 mg of salt a day and limit fluids to about 2 liters. We will check your blood work on the 21st of October.

Call the clinic if you gain 3 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week. Go to the emergency room if you become short of breath at rest or get chest pain. You will return in 1 week to check your weight and swelling.
